title: Norilsk Smelter Dead Zone
summary: Decades of Soviet-era copper-nickel smelting at Norilsk deposited sulfur dioxide and heavy metals across several thousand square kilometers of Siberian taiga and tundra, killing virtually all vegetation downwind. The industrial complex itself continues to operate, but the surrounding ecological zone — forest, wetland, and river systems — was effectively erased. Remediation attempts were minimal and the dead zone persists.

facts.label: Dead zone extent
facts.value: ~24,000 km² of near-zero vegetation (NASA MODIS); ~5,000 km² of fully dead forest stands

facts.label: Peak SO₂ emissions
facts.value: ~2 million tonnes/year (1990s–2000s), largest single point-source on Earth

facts.label: Soil contamination
facts.value: Copper up to 5,000 mg/kg (250× background); nickel up to 3,800 mg/kg near smelters

facts.label: Old Nickel Plant closure
facts.value: 2016; removed ~100,000 t SO₂/year from urban emissions

facts.label: Sulphur capture programme
facts.value: ~$3.5 billion USD committed post-2016; target 75% SO₂ reduction by 2025
